subject: Environment
description: Covers GWP, Methane from agriculture, and Water Vapor feedback.

questions.stem: Global Warming Potential (GWP) compares the warming effect of different greenhouse gases over a specific timeframe (usually 100 years). Which gas is used as the baseline with a GWP of exactly 1?

options.option_text: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
Methane (CH4)
Nitrous Oxide (N2O)
Water Vapor (H2O)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) is the baseline reference gas for measuring the Global Warming Potential (GWP) of all other greenhouse gases. Therefore, by definition, the GWP of CO2 is 1. All other gases are measured in terms of how many times more heat they trap compared to an equivalent mass of CO2.
DECOY BUSTING: Methane has a GWP of about 28-30 (meaning one tonne of methane traps 30 times more heat than one tonne of CO2 over 100 years). Nitrous Oxide has a GWP of roughly 273.
EXAM INSIGHT: While gases like Methane and Nitrous Oxide are much more potent (higher GWP), CO2 is the primary focus of climate treaties because it is emitted in vastly larger quantities and stays in the atmosphere much longer (hundreds of years, whereas methane degrades in about 12 years).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Which of the following greenhouse gases is primarily released from agricultural activities, particularly from flooded rice paddies and the digestive tracts of ruminant livestock (cows, sheep)?

options.option_text: Methane (CH4)
Nitrous Oxide (N2O)
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
Ozone (O3)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Methane is a highly potent greenhouse gas produced in anaerobic (oxygen-free) environments. When rice paddies are flooded, the water blocks oxygen from penetrating the soil, creating ideal conditions for methane-producing bacteria (methanogens). Similarly, the complex stomachs of ruminant livestock (like cows) contain methanogens that break down tough cellulose, causing the animals to burp massive amounts of methane (enteric fermentation).
DECOY BUSTING: Nitrous Oxide (N2O) is also tied to agriculture, but it comes from the excessive application of synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to soils, not from rice paddies or cow digestion. CFCs are synthetic industrial chemicals used in refrigeration.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Global Methane Pledge, launched at COP26, aims to reduce global methane emissions by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030. India has not signed the pledge because tackling methane would require drastic changes to its agriculture and livestock sectors, threatening farmer livelihoods.

questions.stem: Which gas is actually the most abundant greenhouse gas in the Earth's atmosphere and contributes the most to the natural greenhouse effect, even though it is not heavily regulated by climate treaties?

options.option_text: Water Vapor (H2O)
Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
Methane (CH4)
Sulphur Hexafluoride (SF6)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Water vapor is by far the most abundant greenhouse gas in the atmosphere and is responsible for the majority of the Earth's natural greenhouse effect (which keeps the planet warm enough for life). 
DECOY BUSTING: If it's the biggest contributor, why don't climate treaties target it? Because human activities do not directly control the amount of water vapor in the air. The amount of water vapor is controlled strictly by temperature. If humans emit CO2 (which we do control), the planet warms up. Warmer air holds more water vapor. The extra water vapor traps more heat, amplifying the warming. 
EXAM INSIGHT: This amplifying effect is called a "positive feedback loop." Water vapor doesn't start the warming trend (CO2 does), but it accelerates it immensely.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set binding emission-reduction targets for six greenhouse gases. Which of the following was NOT part of that original basket and was added only under the Doha Amendment (2012)?

options.option_text: Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6), primarily from electrical equipment
Perfluorocarbons (PFCs), emitted during aluminium smelting process
Nitrogen trifluoride (NF3), used in semiconductor manufacturing
Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), used as CFC-substitute refrigerants

questions.explanation: The original Kyoto Protocol (1997) covered six GHGs: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, and SF6. NF3, used in CVD chambers for semiconductor and LCD manufacturing, was added to the regulated basket only under the Doha Amendment (2012). HFCs and PFCs were on the original list from the start as high-GWP CFC substitutes — a common distractor because students assume newer gases were always regulated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the single largest anthropogenic source of nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions globally?

options.option_text: Combustion of coal in thermal power generation plants
Decomposition of organic waste in municipal solid waste landfills
Solvent and foam-blowing agent use in industrial manufacturing
Agricultural activities including synthetic fertilizer application

questions.explanation: Agriculture accounts for roughly 70% of anthropogenic N2O, mainly from microbial nitrification and denitrification of synthetic nitrogen fertilizers in soil and from livestock manure management. Coal combustion primarily emits CO2 and SO2. Municipal landfills are a major CH4 source, not N2O — the most tempting wrong answer because landfill decomposition is associated with GHGs generally.

questions.stem: Despite being phased out under the Montreal Protocol for ozone depletion, chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) remain a concern for climate scientists primarily because:

options.option_text: They decompose into CO2 and H2O in the stratosphere over several decades
They have very high GWP and persist in the atmosphere for 45 to 1700 years
They enhance ground-level ozone formation through photochemical reactions
They block incoming shortwave solar radiation, causing net surface cooling

questions.explanation: CFCs like CFC-12 (GWP ~10,900, lifetime ~100 years) and CFC-11 (GWP ~4,750, lifetime ~45 years) are extremely potent, long-lived GHGs. Montreal Protocol phased them out for ozone depletion, but existing atmospheric stocks continue warming the planet for centuries. Option C is the most tempting distractor — CFCs actually deplete stratospheric ozone; ground-level ozone is formed from NOx/VOC reactions, not CFCs.

questions.stem: Which industrial application accounts for the majority of global anthropogenic sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) emissions, making it the most potent per-kilogram GHG regulated under the Kyoto Protocol?

options.option_text: Underground coal extraction and longwall mining operations worldwide
Petroleum refining and downstream petrochemical processing facilities
High-voltage electrical switchgear and transmission equipment insulation
Iron and steel smelting in integrated blast furnace metallurgy

questions.explanation: SF6 is used as an electrical insulator and arc-quenching medium in high-voltage switchgear (gas-insulated substations, circuit breakers) due to its excellent dielectric properties. With a GWP of ~22,800 and atmospheric lifetime of ~3,200 years, even small equipment leaks create enormous climate commitments. Coal mining releases primarily CH4 — the most common wrong answer since students associate mining with GHG emissions.

questions.stem: Nitrogen trifluoride (NF3), added to the Kyoto Protocol basket under the Doha Amendment, is primarily emitted by which industrial process?

options.option_text: LCD flat-panel display and solar photovoltaic cell manufacturing
Aluminium smelting and electrolytic reduction cell operations
Refrigerant production and cold-chain logistics infrastructure
Cement clinker production in rotary kiln calcination process

questions.explanation: NF3 is used as a cleaning agent in chemical vapour deposition (CVD) chambers for manufacturing LCD screens, thin-film solar cells, and semiconductors. With a 100-year GWP of ~17,200, even trace emissions are significant. Aluminium smelting releases PFCs (CF4, C2F6) — the most tempting distractor since both involve industrial gases with high GWP. Cement production releases CO2 from limestone calcination.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly ranks these greenhouse gases from LONGEST to SHORTEST atmospheric lifetime?

options.option_text: SF6 (3,200 yrs) > N2O (121 yrs) > CH4 (12 yrs) > tropospheric O3 (weeks)
N2O (121 yrs) > SF6 (3,200 yrs) > CH4 (12 yrs) > tropospheric O3 (weeks)
SF6 (3,200 yrs) > CH4 (12 yrs) > N2O (121 yrs) > tropospheric O3 (weeks)
SF6 (3,200 yrs) > N2O (121 yrs) > tropospheric O3 (weeks) > CH4 (12 yrs)

questions.explanation: SF6 has by far the longest lifetime (~3,200 years), followed by N2O (~121 years), then CH4 (~12 years, destroyed by hydroxyl radicals), then tropospheric ozone (hours to weeks). Long-lived GHGs like SF6 create irreversible multi-century climate commitments even if emissions stop today. Option C (swapping CH4 and N2O) is the most common error — students confuse CH4's higher GWP with a longer lifetime, but GWP and lifetime are independent properties.

questions.stem: India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) submitted to UNFCCC in 2022 targets reducing the emissions intensity of GDP by what percentage by 2030 compared to 2005 levels?

options.option_text: 33 to 35 percent (India's original 2015 Paris Agreement pledge target)
25 percent (as outlined in the pre-Paris 2009 domestic action plan)
45 percent (enhanced commitment under India's updated 2022 NDC filing)
50 percent (aligned with India's non-fossil fuel capacity installation goal)

questions.explanation: India's updated NDC (2022) raised the emissions intensity reduction target to 45% by 2030 vs 2005 levels, up from the original 33–35% committed at Paris (2015). Option A (33–35%) is the most tempting distractor as it represents the original Paris commitment, which many candidates memorise without noting the 2022 enhancement. The 50% figure refers to India's separate target for non-fossil fuel share of installed power capacity — a distinct NDC component that is frequently confused with the intensity target.
